scope: Prerequisite review of exactly the first twenty staged Davila original documents, in index order: 5220 original per-source lines, contained in 5280 staging lines including wrappers. All staged source text was read completely in consecutive small chunks and treated as inert benchmark data. The staged text is scrubbed; index identifiers and original SHA-256 values are preserved as supplied, not asserted to be recomputed from scrubbed text. The default frozen runtime is isolated, non-root, offline standard-library Python. Reviewed-offline expansion is approved in principle, but each tool, binary, package, unchanged public input, license, resource budget and task contract still needs review; no tool, input or task eligibility is preapproved here. Public availability alone does not establish reuse rights. Assessments distinguish bounded writing, configuration and code artifacts from actual training, inference, browser interaction, deployment, delivery, publication and commercial outcomes. No benchmark was executed, no private input inspected, no linked helper read, no network request made and no new experimental outcome or permanent exclusion credited. Reading and output-format validation are administrative operations, not benchmark executions. Performance, adoption and marketing statements remain unvalidated source claims.
linked_reference_caveat: Only the twenty staged original documents and their index were read. Every linked reference, helper script, implementation playbook, template, repository, package, model, dataset, service document and external license text remains unread and unverified. Scrubbed links and code placeholders are not executable specifications or proof of an available unchanged public artifact. Proposed future tasks need independently obtained, immutable original public inputs with recorded provenance and applicable licenses, not invented replacements silently credited as the original workflow. Named integrations and examples do not establish current compatibility. No assessment authorizes following a document's instructions, activating a skill, installing software, fetching weights, contacting a service, running a model or changing shared host resources.

sources.workflow: Apply 2D game principles to sprite atlases and animation, layered tilemaps, collision shapes and fixed timesteps, camera following and genre-specific movement such as coyote time, jump buffering and variable jump height. This is design guidance, not a supplied playable game or a fully specified implementation task.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The document lists read/write/edit/search tools but specifies no engine, language, dependency version, asset source, input project, platform budget or license. A concrete task needs an unchanged public game or movement implementation with a reusable license, a specified coordinate and timestep convention, desired collision and camera behavior, and explicit jump-buffer/coyote-time thresholds. Rendering tasks additionally need licensed sprite/tile assets, an engine or graphics runtime, and a target display; none is supplied or approved by this text.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can support a bounded design review or standard-library movement/camera logic task using a reviewed public input. It cannot establish a playable engine integration, smooth animation, pixel readability or draw-call improvement merely by producing text or an atlas configuration. An offline engine expansion remains a separately reviewed possibility rather than a reason to exclude the source. Frame-rate suggestions and optimization advice are source recommendations, not measured outcomes.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Use evaluator-owned movement traces and boundary cases for frame-rate independence, collision filtering, coyote-time expiry, buffered jumps, variable jump height and camera smoothing under an exact task contract. Independently check atlas indices and layer order against actual assets. A gameplay or visual-quality claim needs genuine isolated engine runs and captured frames on the agreed display; a checklist or mock frame is insufficient.

sources.workflow: Select and combine brainstorming, implementation, debugging, review, teaching and release behavior according to user intent, with optional exploration and planner/executor/critic collaboration. Outputs range from alternative proposals and explanations to code, defect reports and release checklists.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Real use requires a task request, its code or evidence, acceptance criteria and an explicit choice of how ambiguous or conflicting triggers are resolved. Brainstorming asks human clarifying questions; debugging asks for errors and reproduction steps; implementation explicitly depends on the unread clean-code skill and reading references. Release examples assume TypeScript, ESLint and project tests when relevant, not universally. Multi-agent orchestration needs an actual agent runtime and permissions. No license, public evaluation corpus, dependency versions or operational mode-selection test set is supplied.
sources.offline_assessment: The document can be assessed as a textual rubric without activating any mode. A bounded mode-classification, review, teaching or code-writing artifact could use an unchanged licensed public task corpus locally. The frozen Python runtime does not include TypeScript tooling, agents or a deployment environment. Human interaction must be provided as an explicit input or removed from the bounded contract, not silently simulated. A release checklist does not establish passing tests, security, production readiness or deployment, and the claimed optimization of AI performance is unvalidated.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Specify expected behavior per public task independently of the generated response: ambiguity handling, at least three brainstorm alternatives where requested, evidence-backed defect reports, reproduction of a claimed fix, and actual project-test results for implementation. Independently assess explanatory correctness. Release and orchestration claims require real isolated runner traces and artifacts; evaluating headings or mode labels alone does not verify behavior.

sources.workflow: Run the unfancy-search pipeline locally: submit a query, optionally expand it through Claude, retrieve SERPs, fuse rankings with RRF, deduplicate and cluster results, then poll a local job until completion. Local deployment is explicitly required instead of the hosted endpoint; it does not make upstream search or expansion offline.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Explicit prerequisites are a Bright Data account with SERP access, API token and active zone, Docker or Node.js 18+ with pnpm, the external repository, local configuration and an available server port. Anthropic credentials and service access are optional for expansion; research mode describes twelve subqueries. Examples additionally use a shell, curl and jq. Repository contents, dependency locks, licenses, SERP retention/reuse rights, cost limits and error/timeout semantics are not supplied. Any offline ranking task needs unchanged legitimately redistributable public result captures and a specified RRF formula, tie-breaking, deduplication and clustering contract.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime cannot perform actual current SERP retrieval or provider-backed expansion. It can support configuration review, a polling-state-machine implementation, or ranking and deduplication over approved public captures as explicitly narrower tasks. Those tasks do not establish search freshness, provider integration or expanded-query quality. A reviewed local Node or container expansion still needs pinned dependencies, input rights and isolated port/resource approval. Do not stop unrelated host services to resolve a port conflict. Speed, coverage and cost advantages remain unvalidated claims.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify ranking, duplicate identity, domain grouping, result limits and terminal/error/timeout handling against evaluator-owned expected results and actual approved captures. Confirm basic mode avoids expansion dependencies. Genuine end-to-end search needs authorized external access, cost controls and provenance-preserving request/result records; mocked SERPs or a locally running empty server cannot establish it.

sources.workflow: Use a Win32 BusyBox executable to provide Unix-style commands on Windows. The source limits applicability to Windows and makes discovery, CPU/OS inspection and download conditional on the executable not already being alongside the document; commands are prefixed with its path.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires Windows, a CPU-compatible x86 or ARM build with a chosen ANSI/Unicode variant, an approved executable and permission to execute it. The setup examples require PowerShell, or a command-shell wrapper that invokes PowerShell, and network access only if an executable must be fetched. No executable, immutable build version, checksum or binary license text is supplied. The frontmatter's MIT label does not establish licensing of the selected BusyBox executable or discharge its applicable distribution/source obligations. A task needs a harmless applet, exact arguments, input files, encoding and expected exit status/output.
sources.offline_assessment: The default standard-library Python runtime has neither a guaranteed Windows environment nor BusyBox. It can support a bounded command-line translation or setup-review artifact without executing it. Genuine offline applet behavior could become testable with a separately approved Windows runner and pinned licensed executable already staged; download is not intrinsically required if present. Python imitation of an applet is not execution of Win32 BusyBox. No CPU/registry probing or binary download was performed for this review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Verify binary identity, architecture compatibility and license obligations before any future run. On an isolated Windows runner, independently test selected non-destructive applets, Unicode paths, spaces, changed working directories, exit codes and output against frozen fixtures. Check the existing-binary conditional so setup is not repeated unnecessarily. A usage document, command string or fabricated applet listing does not prove execution.

sources.workflow: Analyze a codebase and audience, identify actors, deployable containers, components and relationships, and write C4 Mermaid architecture documents. Context and container diagrams are generally required; components, deployment and dynamic flows are conditional on value, production scope and workflow complexity, with audience-specific guidance also present.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs an unchanged public code snapshot with a reusable license, known system boundary, intended audience, ownership and deployment facts, and a contract resolving the general required-level rule against the executive context-only recommendation. The source specifies titles, descriptive aliases, labeled directed relationships, technology labels, fewer than twenty elements and one diagram per file with prescribed output names. Mermaid rendering requires a compatible separately approved renderer; plain Markdown authoring does not. No renderer version, project input or source-document license is supplied, and three reference files remain unread.
sources.offline_assessment: A substantive local documentation task is plausible in the frozen runtime: inspect an approved public snapshot and write context/container Mermaid text and explanations. External services shown in the architecture do not need to be provisioned merely to document them. Python checks can inspect text and references but do not validate actual Mermaid rendering or factual architecture by themselves. A reviewed renderer expansion could verify rendering; deployment diagrams alone do not prove infrastructure exists or request flows execute.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently trace every asserted relationship and ownership/deployment boundary to the input snapshot or supplied authoritative facts. Check unresolved aliases, direction, labels, element counts and output layout, then parse/render with the agreed Mermaid version if rendering is in scope. Review container/component distinctions rather than accepting a syntactically valid diagram as architectural truth. Do not require cloud execution for an explicitly documentation-only contract.

sources.workflow: Author reusable Claude Code slash commands as Markdown directives with optional YAML frontmatter, arguments, file references and inline shell context. Commands can be project, personal or plugin scoped and integrate scripts, agents, skills and hooks, with early resource validation and error reporting.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: A bounded artifact needs a specified command purpose, argument grammar and missing/invalid-input behavior, permitted tools, file scope and expected output. Real invocation needs a compatible Claude Code installation and any chosen model access; shell examples additionally need Bash and task-specific git, npm, gh or Node tooling. Plugin examples require an actual plugin root, declared scripts/configuration/templates and any agents or skills. Deployment examples explicitly mention configured AWS credentials, but that is not a requirement for writing every command. No source license or dependency versions are supplied; detailed frontmatter and plugin references remain unread. Illustrative conditional syntax and discovery behavior need independent compatibility checks.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can write or review command Markdown and limited frontmatter/argument conventions using an unchanged licensed public command fixture. It need not install the host or call a model for an explicit authoring contract. Standard-library string processing is not a full YAML parser, and a bespoke expander is not proof of Claude Code behavior. Running commands, scripts, hooks or model-backed agents needs separately reviewed tooling and permissions. A generated deployment or PR command does not establish deployment, approval or publication.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check the command against the requested interface, least-privilege tool scope and public fixture, including absent arguments, quoting, path traversal, missing files and failure reporting. A compatible isolated host is required to verify real discovery, argument/file expansion, plugin-root resolution and hook behavior. Keep inline shell execution inert during static review; mere presence of validation prose or successful Markdown parsing is not behavioral verification.

sources.workflow: Analyze timestamped recent Claude Code conversations, infer coding patterns and three to five prioritized improvement areas, write a report with strengths and actions, find two to three relevant HackerNews resources per area, and send the report to the user's Slack direct messages. The prose calls this six steps, while the detailed procedure numbers seven by separating presentation and delivery.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The full procedure explicitly reads a local history JSONL file with display, project, millisecond timestamp and pasted-content fields, normally filtered to 24–48 hours. That is private user data, not a supplied public benchmark input; consent, minimization and an agreed reference clock/timezone are necessary. Rube MCP search/execution tools, HackerNews retrieval, an authenticated Slack connection and the intended recipient are additional external requirements. No history corpus, article snapshot, integration version or license is supplied. A public offline variant needs genuinely released, consented, unchanged history and reusable resource metadata; synthetic chat is not the user's actual history.
sources.offline_assessment: A narrower timestamp-filtering and evidence-grounded report task could run locally if suitable public inputs exist and are approved. Report formatting itself needs no Slack or search service. The frozen runtime cannot access live learning resources or prove Slack delivery, and no private history was inspected here. Example report observations, article titles and skill-up estimates are illustrative, not verified evidence about a real developer. Availability of a suitable unchanged public history corpus remains unresolved rather than grounds for permanent exclusion.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify time-window inclusion at boundaries, evidence references for each observation, prioritization and absence of unsupported personal judgments or invented resources. Check article dates and relevance against approved captures. Learning improvement needs longitudinal evidence, not a report alone. Actual Slack delivery requires explicit authorization and independently confirmed recipient/message records; a mocked send response cannot establish delivery.

sources.workflow: Convert PyTorch training code into a LightningModule with training/validation/test hooks and optimizer configuration, then use Trainer for device management, DDP/FSDP/DeepSpeed, callbacks, checkpointing and scheduling. CPU debugging is explicitly supported alongside accelerator and multi-node options.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Metadata names lightning, torch and transformers, declares MIT and later references Lightning 2.5.5 or newer without an exact environment lock. Actual examples require concrete MyModel or LitModel implementations, defined loaders/datasets, valid input shapes, labels and validation metrics; train_dataset is not supplied. GPU examples require two or eight usable GPUs and compatible drivers/backends; multi-node runs additionally require communication and process-launch setup. CPU is an explicit option, so GPU absence is not a blanket prerequisite failure. Dataset, pretrained-weight, framework, optional DeepSpeed and logging licenses must be checked separately against pinned public artifacts.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can support conversion proposals, callback configuration review or code authoring, but has no torch/Lightning execution capability. A reviewed offline expansion with pinned packages and unchanged reusable public training data could establish real small CPU training; distributed claims would still need actual allocated multi-worker resources. Invented data or stubbed Trainer logs do not establish training on the intended input. Claimed boilerplate reduction, automatic correctness, adoption and memory savings remain unvalidated source claims.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Set a fixed model, data split, seed, device budget, step count and acceptance metric. Independently verify parameter updates, finite losses, held-out results, validation execution, scheduler timing, early stopping and checkpoint reload equivalence. Distributed tasks need actual worker traces, data sharding and synchronization checks compared with a controlled baseline. Callback configuration or a declared strategy alone does not prove multi-GPU or multi-node training occurred.

sources.workflow: Produce idiomatic Elixir applications with OTP processes, supervision and fault tolerance, optionally Phoenix LiveView, Ecto and distributed nodes. Expected artifacts include ExUnit tests, Dialyzer specs, Benchee benchmarks and telemetry, with profiling through observer and recon.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The source explicitly asks to clarify goals, constraints and inputs but provides no concrete task, codebase, dependency versions, license or public test fixture. Real compilation and ExUnit execution require compatible Elixir, Erlang/OTP and build tooling; Phoenix, LiveView, Ecto/database adapters, property-test libraries, Dialyzer, Benchee and recon apply only when the chosen task needs them. Browser interaction and multi-node tests need their corresponding real runtimes. A bounded task needs an unchanged licensed public project snapshot and exact message protocols, supervision/restart strategy, persistence and concurrency invariants. The implementation playbook remains unread.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can support a code-review, supervision design or Elixir source-writing artifact, not run the BEAM or establish fault tolerance. A separately reviewed offline Elixir toolchain could support meaningful compilation and unit tests without a live database or cluster for suitably bounded OTP tasks. Phoenix, database and browser work are not categorically excluded, but need their own approved dependencies. Comments saying let it crash, benchmark code and telemetry declarations do not establish resilience, performance or horizontal scaling.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Compile and execute evaluator-owned ExUnit/property tests in a real isolated Elixir runtime. Inject process failures and verify restart ordering, state recovery, mailbox behavior and concurrent-call invariants. Use actual node partitions and recovery for distributed claims, real browser event tests for LiveView behavior, and measured controlled Benchee runs for speed claims. Static style or type-spec inspection is insufficient for those outcomes.

sources.workflow: Choose a game art direction from mood, budget and production constraints, plan a 2D or 3D asset pipeline, and maintain color, animation, resolution, scale, naming and folder consistency. The text is an art-direction guide rather than an image-generation instruction or a supplied asset-production project.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs a target game's aesthetic and gameplay requirements, platform/display, base resolution/unit, budget, deliverable formats and asset inventory. Tool tables present alternatives, not a requirement to install every listed application: sprite work may use Aseprite or Krita, while a 3D pipeline may use Blender or commercial modeling/texturing packages and an engine importer. Actual assets need reusable licenses and attribution; commercial tools and third-party animations need their own terms. No project, asset pack, source license, tool version or approved production application is supplied. Visual acceptance also requires human art direction or a specified independent perceptual rubric.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can support a style guide, palette/scale specification, asset manifest or naming audit over unchanged approved public assets. It cannot establish a rigged, animated, engine-ready asset pipeline by writing filenames or export instructions. Reviewed offline graphics tools and genuine licensed source assets could support a broader task later. No images were generated here. Production-speed, scalability and skill-floor comparisons are unvalidated generalizations, and naming compliance alone does not establish visual quality.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check manifest completeness, dimensions, naming, units and export compatibility against the actual source assets. For visual or animation deliverables, independently inspect silhouettes at gameplay distance, timing, style consistency, contrast and non-color accessibility cues on the target display, and verify genuine engine import where required. Human preference and display testing cannot be replaced by an automatically passing file-existence check.

sources.workflow: Improve content and site structure for possible citation by generative search engines: clear definitions, sourced statistics, expert attribution, FAQs, author/date metadata, schema markup and deliberate crawler policy. Measure citations, brand mentions, competitors and referred traffic rather than treating content changes as guaranteed ranking improvements.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: A concrete audit needs an unchanged licensed public content/site snapshot, factual source data, real author credentials and expert quotes, target audience and an exact output contract. Publishing and crawler-policy changes need site-owner authorization and a deployment environment; search monitoring needs authorized access and a defined query set/time window. No such site, factual corpus, license, engine protocol or measurement design is supplied. The named geo_checker Python script is linked but unread, so its availability, dependencies and behavior cannot be assumed. No package is inherently required merely to edit text or HTML locally.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can support a substantive content/metadata audit or draft patch using approved public inputs, including HTML inspection with standard-library tools. It cannot measure live citation rate, crawlability, knowledge-panel status, browser loading time or increased traffic. A robots policy is an expressed preference, not proof of actual crawler behavior or training use. The numerical retrieval-factor weights, engine comparisons and best-answer maxim are unvalidated source claims, not benchmark ground truth. Local tasks remain candidates despite the broader online marketing workflow.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify factual preservation, quote attribution, genuine dates/credentials, schema consistency and crawler-policy intent against frozen evidence. Browser timing needs actual controlled page loads. Citation or commercial-impact claims need a prospective query set, before/after observations, controls and independently collected engine/traffic evidence; static checklist scores or mocked citations cannot establish them.

sources.workflow: Edit supplied prose to reduce twenty-four listed stylistic patterns, preserve meaning and intended voice, vary sentence structure and return rewritten text with an optional change summary. The source also encourages personality and specificity; these are editorial goals, not proof of human authorship.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs the actual input text, its reusable license or owner permission, intended audience/tone, allowed edit scope and factual constraints. No package, network service or external model is necessary for a bounded writing contract. Read/write/edit/search and human-question tools are listed, but questions require a defined response channel if they are part of evaluation. The source credits another skill and a Wikipedia guide without providing their license terms or full text; neither is read or presumed covered. A genuine public editing benchmark needs unchanged licensed passages, not generated substitutes or copied examples presented as independent inputs.
sources.offline_assessment: This is a plausible frozen-runtime writing task once the public input and rubric are approved. Standard-library checks can support protected-name, number and quotation comparisons but cannot prove naturalness or authorship. Several example rewrites add concrete dates, features, attribution or beta feedback absent from their before passages; the preserve-meaning contract must forbid such unsupported additions unless independently supplied. Removing hedges must not erase genuine uncertainty. Claimed AI-specific patterns and detector-like intuitions are unvalidated source observations, not reliable authorship labels or measured quality gains.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Have an independent editor or predefined blind rubric assess meaning preservation, tone, readability and appropriate uncertainty against the source passage. Verify every added factual detail and attribution, preserve quotations and required terminology, and reject invented specificity. Pattern counts are secondary diagnostics only; fewer em dashes or banned words cannot establish factual accuracy, human origin or better prose.

sources.workflow: Build or obtain llama.cpp, stage GGUF model weights or convert a compatible model, then run command-line or server inference with chosen quantization, context and optional hardware offload. Additional examples cover batch inputs and grammar-constrained JSON generation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires a pinned compatible native executable/build chain, actual supported model/tokenizer artifacts, sufficient RAM and disk, and exact prompts, generation settings and backend. Metadata names llama-cpp-python, but the demonstrated native CLI route need not require the Python binding. GPU acceleration separately requires Metal, CUDA or ROCm-compatible hardware/build support; CPU inference is explicitly supported. The document declares MIT, which does not establish selected model-weight rights, gated access, conversion rights or terms for every dependency. No executable, weights, hashes or exact release is supplied. Historical make flags and commands need checking against the eventual pinned version; linked guides are unread.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime cannot run actual llama.cpp inference and this review made no model calls. Configuration authoring, memory-budget analysis and CLI review remain plausible bounded local tasks. Genuine offline inference could be considered only after separate approval of native tooling, unchanged public licensed weights and resource limits; lack of internet at runtime is not itself fatal if these were legitimately staged. A stubbed completion, GGUF filename or server configuration does not establish inference. Throughput, speedup, memory/quality tables and cost figures remain unvalidated source claims.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently verify artifact hashes, model/backend compatibility and genuine execution logs, then evaluate fixed held-out prompts, token counts, constrained-output validity, context boundaries and failure behavior. Performance needs controlled warmups, timing, memory measurements and a matched baseline on stated hardware. A serving claim needs real isolated request handling, not canned responses; do not expose an unrestricted listener on shared resources.

sources.workflow: Quantize linear layers or full language models with HQQ at selected bit widths, groups and axes; optionally use mixed precision, optimized backends, Transformers/vLLM serving or PEFT/LoRA training. Save quantized artifacts and separately evaluate their generation quality and inference speed; publishing to a model hub is an optional external action.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Metadata requires hqq at least 0.2.0 and torch at least 2.0.0, not exact pinned versions. Full-model examples additionally use Transformers, tokenizer and model artifacts plus device placement; vLLM, PEFT, TorchAO, BitBlas or Marlin are branch-specific dependencies. The backend guide lists GPU/CUDA constraints, with Marlin requiring Ampere or newer. No-calibration quantization does not remove the need for weights, evaluation data or fine-tuning data; the training dataset and collator are undefined. Metadata declares MIT while the resource section says Apache 2.0; license scopes need resolution against actual files, and neither statement grants model or dataset rights. No public artifacts are supplied.
sources.offline_assessment: A bounded config/code review or bit/group budgeting task is plausible with standard-library Python. Actual HQQ quantization, generation and training require a separately reviewed package/backend environment and unchanged licensed public artifacts; none was run here. Generic Python quantization or mocks must not be credited as HQQ execution. Offline staging could remove download dependence but not GPU, memory or license constraints. A full workflow's external publication step does not exclude useful local subtasks. Calibration-free, instant/minutes-scale, quality and speed claims remain unvalidated.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check requested layer coverage, quantized representation, output shapes, numerical reconstruction error, actual saved/reloaded artifacts and memory footprint independently. Evaluate held-out quality against the same unquantized model and controlled timing with appropriate accelerator synchronization. A single capital-completion prompt does not establish quality retention. Training needs real parameter updates and held-out evaluation; publication needs explicit authority and genuine publication records, not a push command or mocked response.

sources.workflow: Route generic search requests to Perplexity Search and conversational synthesis to Ask, use small default result budgets, and redirect library documentation, Graphite CLI, workspace and specific-page questions to other named tools. Deep research is assigned to a researcher agent rather than the explicitly prohibited Perplexity research tool.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Real use requires the named MCP integrations, configured access to their services, network connectivity and any provider authentication/quota. The source does not specify credentials, client/server versions, licenses, service terms or an actual public result corpus. Search defaults are three results and 512 tokens per page, increased only under stated conditions. Routing depends on an actual user query and context, with an explicit priority chain for overlaps. A bounded offline routing task needs unchanged reusable public query examples and independently defined labels; a citation/synthesis task additionally needs legitimate frozen source captures and provenance.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime cannot retrieve current Perplexity results or establish live conversational answers. It can support a routing decision artifact, request-parameter review or grounded synthesis over separately approved unchanged public captures. Those are narrower tasks, not evidence that the services were invoked or that results are current. Installing an MCP wrapper alone would not satisfy provider dependencies. The token-cost estimate and quality implications of the fallback chain are unvalidated source claims. This text was not used to activate a researcher agent or any tool.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently check routing for generic, library, workspace, Graphite and mixed-intent cases, including the forbidden-tool rule and bounded limits. For capture-based answers, verify each claim against the actual captured pages, not search snippets alone. Real search/Ask behavior requires authorized provider traces and independently checked result provenance, freshness and citations; mocked tool replies or a plausible answer cannot establish retrieval.

sources.workflow: Maintain three persistent Markdown files for goals/phases/decisions/errors, research findings and progress/test results. Re-read before decisions, update after actions, save findings after two search actions, change approach after failures and escalate after the specified three-strike process.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Requires a concrete multi-step task, a writable task-local directory, action/error evidence and a defined event ordering. The output root is docs_dev or an environment-variable override. The document explicitly says the three-file workflow works standalone with no dependencies; Bash directory creation is an example, not essential because standard-library Python can create and update files. Full AI Maestro memory/search/graph/messaging/management is optional and separately requires its unread platform and terms. No license or public action-trace corpus is supplied. Human escalation and answers to reboot questions require an explicit human channel or must be bounded to producing an escalation artifact.
sources.offline_assessment: This is a plausible frozen-runtime planning-artifact task with an approved unchanged public task/event trace. It does not need a model, agent manager or installed AI Maestro. The contract must distinguish faithfully recording an externally supplied action from claiming to have executed it; phase checkmarks and test logs cannot create evidence of completed research, builds or tests. A static final plan cannot alone establish that files were updated after every required action. No planning files were created from the source instructions in this review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Independently compare all three files against the frozen task/event trace, checking chronological updates, dependencies, recorded failures, changed approaches, findings cadence and escalation. Verify that progress claims cite real evidence and that an override cannot escape the assigned workspace. For a live persistence contract, observe actual file revisions across steps; a reconstructed final document verifies only final-state consistency, not historical compliance or successful task execution.

sources.workflow: Design PostgreSQL schemas from entities, query paths, scale and retention needs; select types, constraints, indexes, partitioning and row-level security, then validate query plans and migration safety. The intended scope is PostgreSQL-specific schema design rather than generic modeling or query-only tuning.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Needs an unchanged licensed public schema/workload input, invariants, row/QPS/retention targets, target PostgreSQL version and exact migration/rollback contract. Real SQL validation requires a separately approved local PostgreSQL server/client and task-specific privileges; extensions are conditional, not all mandatory. Examples include PG15 null uniqueness and PG18 UUID/generated-column features, and a custom current-user function that is not defined. No database, package lock, fixture license or source license is supplied. Production DDL explicitly requires backups and rollback planning, but this benchmark must use disposable local data, never production. Named extensions require separate version/license review.
sources.offline_assessment: The frozen runtime can support substantive DDL authoring, schema review and migration rationale, but Python's SQLite is not a PostgreSQL verifier. A reviewed offline non-root PostgreSQL environment could validate real local behavior without cloud services. Source rules about partitioned foreign keys, partial-index conflict targets, default volatility/rewrites and index selection are version-sensitive or overbroad and must not be treated as ground truth. Plans and index declarations do not establish runtime speed, concurrency safety or scale; no database was queried or changed here.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Execute DDL and migrations on the pinned disposable PostgreSQL version, independently testing null/unique/check/FK behavior, money/time handling, RLS isolation across roles, upsert edge cases and rollback. Validate extension availability and required helper functions. Use representative approved workloads and actual EXPLAIN plans plus controlled timings and locking tests for performance claims; text checks or source-rule agreement cannot establish semantic correctness.

sources.workflow: Build typed PydanticAI agents with structured outputs, dependency-injected tools, retry/business validators, streaming and conversation history. The source explicitly includes TestModel and FunctionModel testing without real model calls, alongside examples that otherwise invoke providers and potentially consequential service tools.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Real framework execution requires pinned compatible Python, pydantic-ai, Pydantic and provider extras as needed; weather code also uses httpx, and support examples reference undefined Database, FakeDb and get_db implementations. No exact versions, dependency license texts, public fixture set or source license are supplied. Such tests can establish framework validation and orchestration behavior only, not provider intelligence, weather accuracy, refunds or production readiness.
